audit.whatIsWrong: Rated 5.5/10 while the win rate is 53.57% and the page's own whys give Karma five of the seven stages.
audit.why: Flamespitter is a 600-range cone; Karma pokes at 950 and Rumble must walk into her to farm. The lane is mildly favoured, not neutral.
audit.corrected: diffRating 4.5/10 and both difficulty lines adjusted.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five rows contradicted their own whys — levels 1, 2, 3, 4-5 and first item were Skill or Rumble while the whys say 'your poke compounds', 'stacked Q/RQ rotations chunk an immobile Rumble', 'your bullying peak' and 'keeping you ahead'. Level 6 was Skill while its why says 'this window is genuinely Rumble's'.
audit.why: Karma owns everything up to first item; The Equalizer at 6 is Rumble's stage; 2+ items is his as well, which the mirror (rumble__karma) already established and which the late text agrees with.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 2, 3 and 5 to Karma and row 4 to Rumble, in matched pairs. Row 6 left as Rumble to stay consistent with the mirror, and whys[6] rewritten so it no longer reads as a Karma stage.

audit.whatIsWrong: The whole page keys commits to Scrap Shield's cooldown, but Scrap Shield is a flat 6 seconds — it is never meaningfully down. The real gate is Rumble's Heat: at 100 he Overheats and cannot cast spells at all. Electro Harpoon was also described only as a slow; it fires from 850 range, carries two charges, and reduces Magic Resist.
audit.why: Telling a player to 'trade just after he burns Scrap Shield' hands them a two-second window on a six-second cooldown. Heat is the actual punishable state, and the MR shred is why his follow-up damage lands harder than the poke maths suggest.
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d and report[5].t now point at Heat and the 6-second shield; wants.foe[1] states the 850 range, both charges and the MR shred; dontsFull[0].d states that The Equalizer cuts a retreat Karma has no dash to answer.

audit.whatIsWrong: The early, mid and late text are written in first person — 'I out-range Rumble hard here', 'my bullying peak', 'my cooldown rhythm' — instead of the site's second-person coaching voice.
audit.why: Every other matchup addresses the player as 'you'; this page reads as someone else's diary and breaks the voice mid-site.
audit.corrected: All three paragraphs rewritten in second person at the same length, with the harpoon range and Overheat detail folded in.

edits.before: I out-range Rumble hard here — his Flamespitter (Q) is a short stubby cone, so he has to walk most of the way into me just to farm, and that's exactly where my Inner Flame (Q) and a level-1 RQ Soulflare zone chunk him for free. Don't stand still poking, though: his Electro Harpoon (E) slows me, and if it lands he'll cling on with Scrap Shield's (W) move speed for a full Flamespitter channel. Throw Q on cooldown, respect the harpoon, and keep Inspire (E) up to shield the slow and walk away — if I poke him to 100 heat he Overheats and silences himself, which is my cleanest punish.
edits.after: You out-range Rumble hard here — his Flamespitter (Q) is a short stubby cone, so he has to walk most of the way into you just to farm, and that's exactly where your Inner Flame (Q) and a level-1 RQ Soulflare zone chunk him for free. Don't stand still poking, though: his Electro Harpoon (E) slows you from 850 and shreds your MR, and if it lands he'll cling on with Scrap Shield's (W) move speed for a full Flamespitter channel. Throw Q on cooldown, respect the harpoon, and keep Inspire (E) up to shield the slow and walk away — poke him to 100 heat and he Overheats, unable to cast, which is your cleanest punish.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are my bullying peak — repeated Q/RQ rotations push him off the wave whenever his heat is low, and Inspire's shield + speed lets me tax plates while he's stuck farming under chip. Level 6 is the catch: The Equalizer (R) is his real spike, a long flame line that covers the exact zone I want to poke from. Bait it or E-speed through it, never sit channeling RQ inside it — once his ult is down the lane is mine again, and Gathering Fire keeps my Mantra coming back faster every time I land a Q.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your bullying peak — repeated Q/RQ rotations push him off the wave whenever his heat is low, and Inspire's shield + speed lets you tax plates while he's stuck farming under chip. Level 6 is the catch: The Equalizer (R) is his real spike, a long flame wall that covers the exact zone you want to poke from and cuts the retreat you have no dash for. Bait it or E-speed through it, never sit inside it — once his ult is down the lane is yours again, and Gathering Fire keeps Mantra coming back faster every Q you land.

edits.before: My first AP/haste item snaps RQ damage and shield uptime back up, and I stay favoured as long as I keep chipping from outside Flamespitter range. But Rumble is an AP bruiser who out-itemizes me — by two-plus items his Danger-Zone Flamespitter DPS plus Equalizer in fights out-damage my single-target chip, and I have no real late teamfight carry of my own. Convert the early-to-first-item lead into towers and roams; don't let this drag into a sustained 1v1 where his flame eventually beats my cooldown rhythm.

notes: Two structural problems fixed. First, the whole page schedules trades around Scrap Shield's cooldown, which is a flat 6 seconds and therefore not a window at all — Rumble's Heat bar (Overheat at 100 = cannot cast) is the real gate, and the page already knew that in spikes[1] but not anywhere in the full layer. Second, early/mid/late were written in first person ('I out-range Rumble hard here'); rewritten to the site's second-person voice at matched length. Row 6 kept as Rumble to agree with the already-audited mirror, with whys[6] rewritten so the row and its reason no longer contradict. The packet's suspectNames for 'Electro Harpoon' and 'Scrap Shield' are false positives — both are Rumble's real ability names.
